Lemma
[Nilpotent subgroups of $\operatorname {Isom}(\mathbb H^n)$] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0198 ↗ def:chow-iv-isometry-types ↗ def:chow-iv-nilpotent-group 1. ch31:31.11\group Discrete groups

If $G\subset \operatorname {Isom}(\mathbb H^n)$ is nilpotent, then either it is trivial, contains a nontrivial elliptic element, all nontrivial elements are hyperbolic with the same two ideal fixed points, or all nontrivial elements are parabolic with one common ideal fixed point.
